questions.skill: Describe the trend of a line graph
questions.stem: A line graph shows the number of customers in a shop. 9 a.m.: 4, 10 a.m.: 9, 11 a.m.: 15, noon: 22, 1 p.m.: 14, 2 p.m.: 8. When does the line go down?
questions.solution: The numbers rise until noon (22). After that they fall to 14 and then 8, so the line goes down from noon to 2 p.m.

solve.work: 4, 9, 15, 22 rising to noon, then 22 -> 14 -> 8 falling from noon to 2 p.m.

questions.skill: Find the greatest change or the steepest part
questions.stem: A line graph shows the water in a tank each hour. 1 p.m.: 40 gallons, 2 p.m.: 52, 3 p.m.: 58, 4 p.m.: 75, 5 p.m.: 80. What was the greatest increase from one hour to the next, in gallons?
questions.solution: The increases are 12, 6, 17 and 5 gallons. The greatest is 17 gallons.

questions.skill: Find the change between two times
questions.stem: A line graph shows a candle getting shorter by the same amount every hour. At 2 p.m. it is 18 cm tall. At 5 p.m. it is 9 cm tall. By how many centimeters does it get shorter each hour?
questions.solution: It lost 18 - 9 = 9 cm in 5 - 2 = 3 hours. 9 / 3 = 3 cm each hour.

solve.work: 18 - 9 = 9 cm over 3 hours, 9 / 3 = 3 cm per hour.

questions.skill: Plan and set up a line graph of data over time
questions.stem: Lena wants a vertical scale for a line graph of these values: 20, 35, 50, 65 and 80. The scale must start at 0 and go up in equal steps, with every value exactly on a mark. Which scale works?
questions.solution: Every value is a multiple of 5, and the top mark of 80 reaches the largest value. Counting by 20s or 15s misses some values, and a top of 60 is too low.

solve.work: All values are multiples of 5 and at most 80, so 0-80 by 5s works. By 15s misses 20; 0-60 stops below 65 and 80; by 20s misses 35 and 65.

questions.skill: Classify survey questions as categorical or numerical
questions.stem: Survey question P: How many minutes did you read yesterday? Survey question Q: What kind of book did you read yesterday? Which statement is true?
choices: P gives categorical data and Q gives numerical data.
P and Q both give numerical data.
P and Q both give categorical data.
P gives numerical data and Q gives categorical data.
questions.answer: P gives numerical data and Q gives categorical data.
questions.solution: Minutes are numbers, so P is numerical. The kind of book is a name, so Q is categorical.

solve.answer: P gives numerical data and Q gives categorical data.
solve.work: Minutes read is numerical; kind of book is categorical.

questions.skill: Describe the trend of a line graph
questions.stem: A line graph shows the temperature on five days. Monday: 70, Tuesday: 74, Wednesday: 68, Thursday: 72, Friday: 79. On how many days was the temperature higher than on the day before?
questions.solution: Tuesday (74 > 70), Thursday (72 > 68) and Friday (79 > 72) are higher than the day before. Wednesday is lower. That is 3 days.

solve.work: Tue 74>70 yes, Wed 68<74 no, Thu 72>68 yes, Fri 79>72 yes: 3 days.

questions.skill: Decide when a line graph fits the data
questions.stem: Which data should be shown on a line graph, not a bar graph?
choices: The number of pets owned by each of five families
The number of students who chose each of the four school lunches
The number of visitors to a zoo in each month of a year
The heights of six different buildings
questions.answer: The number of visitors to a zoo in each month of a year
questions.solution: The zoo data follows one thing as time passes, so a line graph fits. The other data compare separate groups, which a bar graph shows better.

solve.answer: The number of visitors to a zoo in each month of a year
solve.work: Zoo visitors each month of a year changes over time; the others compare separate categories.

questions.skill: Find the greatest change or the steepest part
questions.stem: Savings by week: Week 1: 15 dollars, Week 2: 25 dollars, Week 3: 30 dollars, Week 4: 50 dollars, Week 5: 55 dollars. Which statement is true?
choices: The savings rose by 20 dollars from Week 3 to Week 4.
The savings rose by 20 dollars from Week 1 to Week 2.
The savings rose by 5 dollars from Week 3 to Week 4.
The savings rose by 20 dollars from Week 4 to Week 5.
questions.answer: The savings rose by 20 dollars from Week 3 to Week 4.
questions.solution: From Week 3 to Week 4 the savings went from 30 to 50, a rise of 20 dollars. From Week 1 to Week 2 the rise was 10, and from Week 4 to Week 5 it was 5.

solve.answer: The savings rose by 20 dollars from Week 3 to Week 4.
solve.work: Rises: W1-2 10, W2-3 5, W3-4 20, W4-5 5. Only Week 3 to Week 4 = 20 is true.

questions.skill: Plan and set up a line graph of data over time
questions.stem: On a line graph of a plant's height, one point is at (5, 18). The first number is the week and the second number is the height in centimeters. What does this point show?
choices: In Week 18, the plant was 5 cm tall.
The plant grew 5 cm in 18 weeks.
The plant grew 18 cm during Week 5.
In Week 5, the plant was 18 cm tall.
questions.answer: In Week 5, the plant was 18 cm tall.
questions.solution: The first number is the week, 5, and the second is the height, 18 cm. So in Week 5 the plant was 18 cm tall.

solve.answer: In Week 5, the plant was 18 cm tall.
solve.work: (week, height) = (5, 18): in Week 5 the plant was 18 cm tall.

questions.skill: Find the greatest change or the steepest part
questions.stem: A line graph shows the number of fish in a tank at the start of each month. January: 40, February: 52, March: 48, April: 60. Add up the rises only, ignoring the drop. By how many fish does the graph rise in total?
questions.solution: The rises are 52 - 40 = 12 (January to February) and 60 - 48 = 12 (March to April). The drop in March is ignored. 12 + 12 = 24.

solve.work: Rises: Jan-Feb +12, Mar-Apr +12; drop Feb-Mar ignored. Total 24.

questions.skill: Plan and set up a line graph of data over time
questions.stem: Which question collects data that changes over time and can be shown on a line graph?
choices: What is your favorite kind of tree in the park?
How tall is the tree in the park at the end of each month?
How many trees are in each park in town?
Which tree in the park is the tallest?
questions.answer: How tall is the tree in the park at the end of each month?
questions.solution: Only the first question measures the same thing again and again over time, so its data can be plotted on a line graph.

solve.answer: How tall is the tree in the park at the end of each month?
solve.work: Height of one tree at the end of each month changes over time.

questions.skill: Counting cubes in layers
questions.stem: A box is filled with unit cubes. Each layer has 6 unit cubes and the box has 3 layers. What is the volume of the box in cubic units?
questions.solution: There are 3 layers with 6 cubes in each. $6 \times 3 = 18$ unit cubes, so the volume is 18 cubic units.

solve.work: 6 cubes per layer x 3 layers = 18 cubic units.

questions.skill: Recognizing volume and cubic units
questions.stem: What does the volume of a solid measure?
choices: The length of its longest edge
The amount of space inside the solid
The amount of flat surface it covers
questions.answer: The amount of space inside the solid
questions.solution: Volume is the amount of space a solid takes up. Edge length and the distance around are lengths, and flat surface is area.

solve.answer: The amount of space inside the solid
solve.work: Volume is the amount of space a solid occupies/encloses.

questions.skill: Recognizing volume and cubic units
questions.stem: A unit cube has edges that are each 1 centimeter long. What is the volume of one unit cube?
questions.solution: A cube with 1 centimeter edges is the unit of volume called 1 cubic centimeter. A square centimeter measures flat area and a centimeter measures length.

solve.work: A cube with 1 cm edges has volume 1 cubic centimeter by definition.

questions.skill: Volume of a figure built from cube towers
questions.stem: A figure is built from three towers of unit cubes standing side by side. The towers have 2 cubes, 3 cubes and 4 cubes. What is the volume of the figure in cubic units?
questions.solution: Each unit cube has a volume of 1 cubic unit, so add the cubes in the towers: $2 + 3 + 4 = 9$ cubic units.

questions.skill: Recognizing volume and cubic units
questions.stem: Which measurement could be the volume of a toy box?
questions.solution: Volume is measured in cubic units such as cubic feet. Feet measure length, square feet measure area and degrees measure angles.

solve.work: Volume is measured in cubic units; only 9 cubic feet is a volume.

questions.skill: Comparing volumes by counting cubes
questions.stem: Tank A holds 15 unit cubes and Tank B holds 22 unit cubes when each is completely full. How many more cubic units of volume does Tank B have than Tank A?
questions.solution: Compare the number of cubes: $22 - 15 = 7$. Tank B has 7 more cubic units.

questions.skill: Comparing volumes by counting cubes
questions.stem: Box P and Box Q are both filled with the same kind of unit cube. Box P holds 18 cubes and Box Q holds 24 cubes. Which box has the greater volume?
choices: Box P, because 18 is the smaller number
Box Q, because it holds more unit cubes
Box P, because it needs fewer cubes
They are equal, because the cubes are the same
questions.answer: Box Q, because it holds more unit cubes
questions.solution: The cubes are the same size, so the box that holds more cubes has more volume. 24 is more than 18, so Box Q has the greater volume.

solve.answer: Box Q, because it holds more unit cubes
solve.work: Same-size cubes, so more cubes means more volume: Q holds 24 > 18.

questions.skill: Cubes needed to fill a container
questions.stem: A box can hold 20 unit cubes when it is full. Right now it has 12 unit cubes in it. How many more unit cubes are needed to fill it?
questions.solution: The box needs $20 - 12 = 8$ more unit cubes.

questions.skill: Recognizing volume and cubic units
questions.stem: To measure volume by counting cubes, how must the cubes fill the solid?
choices: With gaps so the cubes can move
With cubes of many different sizes
With no gaps and no overlaps
questions.answer: With no gaps and no overlaps
questions.solution: To count volume, the same-size cubes must pack the solid completely, with no gaps between them and no cubes sharing the same space.

solve.answer: With no gaps and no overlaps
solve.work: Counting unit cubes measures volume only when packed with no gaps or overlaps.

questions.skill: Counting cubes in layers
questions.stem: A box is 5 unit cubes long, 2 unit cubes wide and 1 unit cube tall. How many unit cubes fill it?
questions.solution: The box has one layer of 2 rows with 5 cubes in each row. $5 \times 2 = 10$ unit cubes.

solve.work: 5 x 2 = 10 cubes in one layer, 1 layer tall: 10 cubes.

questions.skill: Counting cubes in layers
questions.stem: The bottom layer of a box has 3 rows of 5 unit cubes. The box is filled exactly with 4 layers like this. What is the volume of the box in cubic units?
questions.solution: One layer has $3 \times 5 = 15$ cubes. Four layers hold $15 \times 4 = 60$ cubes, so the volume is 60 cubic units.

solve.work: Bottom layer 3 x 5 = 15 cubes; 4 layers: 60 cubic units.

questions.skill: Measuring with improvised units
questions.stem: Kai fills a box with small blocks and counts 48 blocks. Pia fills the same box with larger blocks and counts 12 blocks. Which statement is true?
choices: Each of Pia's blocks takes up more space than each of Kai's blocks
Each of Kai's blocks takes up more space than each of Pia's blocks
Pia's box has a smaller volume than Kai's box
Pia and Kai's blocks are the same size
questions.answer: Each of Pia's blocks takes up more space than each of Kai's blocks
questions.solution: The box is the same, so it holds the same amount of space. It takes fewer of Pia's blocks to fill it, so each of her blocks must take up more space.

solve.answer: Each of Pia's blocks takes up more space than each of Kai's blocks
solve.work: Same box, fewer blocks needed by Pia (12 vs 48), so each of her blocks is larger (4 times Kai's). Volume of the box is the same.

questions.skill: Volume of a figure built from cube towers
questions.stem: A figure is built from five towers of unit cubes in a row. The towers have 1, 3, 4, 3 and 1 cubes. What is the volume of the figure in cubic units?
questions.solution: Add the cubes in each tower: $1 + 3 + 4 + 3 + 1 = 12$ cubic units.

questions.skill: Comparing volumes by counting cubes
questions.stem: Four boxes are filled with unit cubes. Which box has the greatest volume?
questions.solution: Find the cubes in each box: $3 \times 9 = 27$, $4 \times 6 = 24$, $2 \times 12 = 24$ and $5 \times 5 = 25$. The greatest is 27, so the box with 3 layers of 9 cubes.

questions.skill: Measuring with improvised units
questions.stem: A box holds 36 small blocks. One large block takes up the same space as 3 small blocks. How many large blocks fill the same box exactly?
questions.solution: Each large block covers 3 small blocks of space. $36 \div 3 = 12$ large blocks.

questions.skill: Cubes needed to fill a container
questions.stem: A crate holds 6 layers of 8 unit cubes when it is full. It now holds 29 unit cubes. How many more unit cubes are needed to fill it?
questions.solution: A full crate holds $6 \times 8 = 48$ cubes. It needs $48 - 29 = 19$ more.

questions.skill: Counting cubes in layers
questions.stem: A box is filled with 3 layers of unit cubes. Each layer has 4 rows of 6 cubes. Which expression gives the number of unit cubes in the box?
questions.solution: Each layer has $4 \times 6$ cubes and there are 3 layers, so the total is $3 \times 4 \times 6$.

solve.work: Each layer 4 x 6 cubes, 3 layers: 3 x 4 x 6 = 72.

questions.skill: Cubes needed to fill a container
questions.stem: A box has a volume of 24 cubic units. Each of its layers holds 6 unit cubes. How many layers does it have?
questions.solution: Each layer holds 6 cubes and the box holds 24 cubes, so there are $24 \div 6 = 4$ layers.

questions.skill: Measuring with improvised units
questions.stem: Box X and Box Y are each filled exactly with 20 blocks. The blocks used for Box Y are larger than the blocks used for Box X. Which statement is true?
choices: Box Y has a greater volume than Box X
Box X has a greater volume than Box Y
Box X and Box Y have the same volume
Box Y has a smaller volume because its blocks are larger
questions.answer: Box Y has a greater volume than Box X
questions.solution: Both boxes use 20 blocks, but each block of Box Y takes up more space. So 20 of them take up more space and Box Y has the greater volume.

solve.answer: Box Y has a greater volume than Box X
solve.work: Same number of blocks but Y's blocks are larger, so Y holds more space.

questions.skill: Counting cubes in layers
questions.stem: A cube-shaped box is 3 unit cubes long, 3 unit cubes wide and 3 unit cubes tall. How many unit cubes fill it?
questions.solution: One layer has $3 \times 3 = 9$ cubes, and there are 3 layers. $9 \times 3 = 27$ unit cubes.

questions.skill: Counting cubes in layers
questions.stem: A solid has 4 layers. Each layer is 5 unit cubes long and 3 unit cubes wide. A tunnel is then cut straight through the solid from top to bottom by removing 1 cube from every layer. How many unit cubes are left?
questions.solution: The full solid has $5 \times 3 = 15$ cubes in a layer, so $15 \times 4 = 60$ cubes. The tunnel removes 4 cubes, leaving $60 - 4 = 56$ unit cubes.

solve.work: Each layer 5 x 3 = 15; 4 layers = 60. Tunnel removes 1 cube from each of 4 layers: 60 - 4 = 56.

questions.skill: Measuring with improvised units
questions.stem: A box is filled with 96 small cubes. One large cube takes up the same space as 8 small cubes. Dana fills exactly half of the box using large cubes. How many large cubes does she use?
questions.solution: Half of the box is $96 \div 2 = 48$ small cubes of space. Each large cube covers 8 small cubes, so she uses $48 \div 8 = 6$ large cubes.

solve.work: Half the box = 48 small cubes of space. 48 / 8 = 6 large cubes.

questions.skill: Measuring with improvised units
questions.stem: Container P holds 40 small cubes. Container Q holds 15 large cubes, and each large cube takes up the same space as 3 small cubes. Which container has the greater volume?
choices: Container P, because 40 is greater than 15
Container P, because 15 large cubes equal 35 small cubes
They are equal, because both are full of cubes
Container Q, because 15 large cubes equal 45 small cubes
questions.answer: Container Q, because 15 large cubes equal 45 small cubes
questions.solution: Change Q to small cubes: $15 \times 3 = 45$. Since 45 is more than 40, Container Q has the greater volume.

solve.answer: Container Q, because 15 large cubes equal 45 small cubes
solve.work: Q: 15 x 3 = 45 small cubes > 40, so Q is greater.

questions.skill: Volume of a figure built from cube towers
questions.stem: A solid is built on a base that is 3 rows of 4 cubes. In front, the first row of 4 towers is 1 cube high, the second row is 2 cubes high and the third row is 3 cubes high. How many unit cubes make the solid?
questions.solution: Each row has 4 towers. The rows hold $4 \times 1 = 4$, $4 \times 2 = 8$ and $4 \times 3 = 12$ cubes. The total is $4 + 8 + 12 = 24$.

solve.issues: Wording "In front, the first row of 4 towers" is slightly awkward but the meaning is clear.
solve.work: Three rows of 4 towers with heights 1, 2, 3: 4x1 + 4x2 + 4x3 = 4 + 8 + 12 = 24.

questions.skill: Counting cubes in layers
questions.stem: Zoe counted the 12 unit cubes in the bottom layer of a box and said its volume is 12 cubic units. The box is filled with 5 layers like the bottom layer. What mistake did she make?
choices: She counted the layers instead of the cubes
She counted only one layer instead of all 5
She should have used square units
questions.answer: She counted only one layer instead of all 5
questions.solution: The volume is the number of cubes in the whole box. All 5 layers hold 12 cubes each, so the volume is $12 \times 5 = 60$ cubic units. She counted only one layer.

solve.answer: She counted only one layer instead of all 5
solve.work: Full box is 5 layers of 12 = 60; she counted only the bottom layer.

questions.skill: Cubes needed to fill a container
questions.stem: A box is filled exactly with 90 unit cubes in 5 layers. Every layer has 6 cubes in each row. How many rows does each layer have?
questions.solution: Each layer has $90 \div 5 = 18$ cubes. With 6 cubes in each row, there are $18 \div 6 = 3$ rows.

questions.skill: Comparing volumes by counting cubes
questions.stem: A box is filled with 4 layers of 15 unit cubes. Which box has the same volume?
questions.solution: The first box has $4 \times 15 = 60$ cubes. Of the other boxes, $6 \times 10 = 60$ matches, while $5 \times 14 = 70$, $4 \times 11 = 44$ and $3 \times 15 = 45$ do not.

questions.skill: Volume of a figure built from cube towers
questions.stem: A solid sits on a square base of 3 by 3 towers. The 4 corner towers are each 1 cube high, the 4 edge towers are each 2 cubes high, and the center tower is 4 cubes high. What is the volume of the solid in cubic units?
questions.solution: Corners: $4 \times 1 = 4$ cubes. Edges: $4 \times 2 = 8$ cubes. Center: 4 cubes. The total is $4 + 8 + 4 = 16$ cubic units.

solve.work: Corners 4 x 1 = 4, edges 4 x 2 = 8, center 4: total 16.

questions.skill: Cubes needed to fill a container
questions.stem: Ava fills a box exactly with 72 cubes that each have 1 centimeter edges. She places them in layers. Which could be the length, width and height of the box?
questions.solution: The volume is 72 cubic centimeters. $6 \times 4 \times 3 = 72$ matches. The others give $48$, $60$ and $54$.

solve.issues: Leans on the length x width x height formula (NC.5.MD.5) more than counting cubes, but still fits filling with cm cubes in layers.

questions.skill: Measuring with improvised units
questions.stem: Ella fills a bin exactly with 150 identical blocks. The bin has a volume of 1,200 cubic centimeters. What is the volume of one block, in cubic centimeters?
questions.solution: The 150 blocks share the 1,200 cubic centimeters equally. $1200 \div 150 = 8$ cubic centimeters for each block.

solve.work: 150 blocks fill 1,200 cubic cm, so each is 1200 / 150 = 8 cubic cm.

questions.skill: Volume by layers
questions.stem: A box is packed with unit cubes in layers. Each layer has 12 cubes and there are 3 layers. How many unit cubes are in the box?
questions.solution: Each layer has 12 cubes and there are 3 layers, so the box holds $12 \times 3 = 36$ unit cubes.

questions.skill: Volume formula length x width x height
questions.stem: A rectangular prism is 4 centimeters long, 3 centimeters wide, and 2 centimeters tall. What is its volume in cubic centimeters?
questions.solution: Volume is length times width times height: $4 \times 3 \times 2 = 24$ cubic centimeters.

questions.skill: Volume formula length x width x height
questions.stem: A rectangular prism has length 5, width 2, and height 3. Which expression gives its volume?
questions.solution: The volume of a rectangular prism is length times width times height, so it is $5 \times 2 \times 3$. Adding the three numbers, or multiplying only two of them, does not count the cubes that fill the prism.

solve.work: V = l x w x h = 5 x 2 x 3 = 30; only the product matches.

questions.skill: Volume by layers
questions.stem: Mia builds a box by stacking layers of unit cubes. Each layer is 5 cubes long and 4 cubes wide. She stacks 2 layers. How many unit cubes does she use?
questions.solution: One layer has $5 \times 4 = 20$ cubes. Two layers have $20 \times 2 = 40$ cubes. The answer 20 forgets the second layer.

questions.skill: Volume formula base area x height
questions.stem: The base of a prism has an area of 10 square centimeters. The prism is 4 centimeters tall. What is its volume in cubic centimeters?
questions.solution: Volume is the area of the base times the height: $10 \times 4 = 40$ cubic centimeters.

questions.skill: Volume of two joined prisms
questions.stem: A toy is made of two rectangular prisms joined together. One has a volume of 12 cubic inches and the other has a volume of 8 cubic inches. What is the volume of the toy in cubic inches?
questions.solution: The volume of the whole toy is the sum of the two parts: $12 + 8 = 20$ cubic inches.

questions.skill: Volume of a cube
questions.stem: A cube has edges that are each 3 inches long. What is its volume in cubic inches?
questions.solution: A cube is a rectangular prism whose length, width and height are all 3 inches, so its volume is $3 \times 3 \times 3 = 27$ cubic inches. The answer 9 is the area of one face.

questions.skill: Volume as addition
questions.stem: Ben counts the cubes in a box layer by layer: $6 + 6 + 6 + 6$. Which multiplication expression gives the same total?
questions.solution: There are 4 layers of 6 cubes each. Adding 6 four times is the same as $4 \times 6$, which is 24.

questions.skill: Volume in a real situation
questions.stem: A sandbox is shaped like a rectangular prism. It is 6 feet long, 5 feet wide, and 2 feet deep. How many cubic feet of sand will fill it?
questions.solution: The volume is $6 \times 5 \times 2 = 60$ cubic feet.

questions.skill: Volume of two joined prisms
questions.stem: A shape is made of two prisms joined together. The prisms have volumes of 15 cubic centimeters and 9 cubic centimeters. What is the volume of the whole shape?
questions.solution: The volume of the whole shape is the sum of the volumes of its two parts: $15 + 9 = 24$ cubic centimeters. Subtracting or multiplying the volumes does not fit joining two solids.

questions.skill: Volume by layers
questions.stem: A packing box holds unit cubes. The bottom layer is 7 cubes by 3 cubes, and the box is filled to 4 layers. How many unit cubes are in the box?
questions.solution: One layer has $7 \times 3 = 21$ cubes. Four layers have $21 \times 4 = 84$ cubes.

questions.skill: Volume formula length x width x height
questions.stem: A shipping box is 8 inches long, 5 inches wide, and 6 inches tall. What is its volume in cubic inches?
questions.solution: $8 \times 5 = 40$, and $40 \times 6 = 240$. The volume is 240 cubic inches.

questions.skill: Volume formula length x width x height
questions.stem: A tank is 10 centimeters long, 4 centimeters wide, and 3 centimeters tall. What is its volume?
questions.solution: Multiply the three measurements: $10 \times 4 \times 3 = 120$ cubic centimeters. Adding them gives 17, and 164 is the surface area, which is a different measure.

questions.skill: Volume formula base area x height
questions.stem: A prism has a base with an area of 15 square meters and a height of 6 meters. What is its volume in cubic meters?
questions.solution: Volume is base area times height: $15 \times 6 = 90$ cubic meters.

questions.skill: Volume formula base area x height
questions.stem: A rectangular prism has a base with area $B$ and a height $h$. Which formula gives its volume $V$?
questions.solution: The volume of a prism is the area of its base times its height, so $V = B \times h$.

questions.skill: Volume of two joined prisms
questions.stem: A shape is made of two rectangular prisms joined together. The first is 4 centimeters long, 3 centimeters wide, and 2 centimeters tall. The second is 5 centimeters long, 2 centimeters wide, and 3 centimeters tall. What is the volume of the whole shape in cubic centimeters?
questions.solution: The first prism has volume $4 \times 3 \times 2 = 24$. The second has volume $5 \times 2 \times 3 = 30$. Together they have $24 + 30 = 54$ cubic centimeters.

questions.skill: Volume of two joined prisms
questions.stem: A step is built from two blocks. The bottom block is 6 feet long, 2 feet wide, and 1 foot tall. A top block, 3 feet long, 2 feet wide, and 1 foot tall, sits on it. What is the volume of the step?
questions.solution: The bottom block has volume $6 \times 2 \times 1 = 12$ cubic feet and the top block has volume $3 \times 2 \times 1 = 6$ cubic feet. Together: $12 + 6 = 18$ cubic feet.

solve.work: Bottom 6 x 2 x 1 = 12; top 3 x 2 x 1 = 6; total 18.

questions.skill: Volume in a real situation
questions.stem: A fish tank is 20 inches long, 10 inches wide, and 12 inches tall. When it is filled to the top, how many cubic inches of water does it hold?
questions.solution: $20 \times 10 = 200$, and $200 \times 12 = 2{,}400$. The tank holds 2,400 cubic inches of water.

questions.skill: Missing dimension from the volume
questions.stem: A rectangular prism has a volume of 48 cubic units. Its bottom layer has 12 unit cubes. How many layers tall is the prism?
questions.solution: Each layer has 12 cubes, and all the layers together make 48. So the number of layers is $48 \div 12 = 4$.

questions.skill: Volume by layers
questions.stem: A box is 5 cubes long, 4 cubes wide, and 3 cubes tall. Mario has filled the bottom layer with unit cubes. How many more unit cubes does he need to fill the box?
questions.solution: One layer has $5 \times 4 = 20$ cubes, and the box has 3 layers, so it holds $20 \times 3 = 60$ cubes in all. He has already put in 20, so he needs $60 - 20 = 40$ more.

solve.work: Total 5 x 4 x 3 = 60; bottom layer 5 x 4 = 20; 60 - 20 = 40 more.

questions.skill: Volume of two joined prisms
questions.stem: A building model is made of two rectangular prisms joined together. The main part is 9 centimeters long, 4 centimeters wide, and 3 centimeters tall. The attached part is 3 centimeters long, 4 centimeters wide, and 5 centimeters tall. What is the volume of the model in cubic centimeters?
questions.solution: The main part has volume $9 \times 4 \times 3 = 108$. The attached part has volume $3 \times 4 \times 5 = 60$. Together: $108 + 60 = 168$ cubic centimeters.

questions.skill: Volume of two joined prisms
questions.stem: A solid is made by gluing two prisms together. The first has a volume of 60 cubic centimeters. The second is 5 centimeters long, 4 centimeters wide, and 3 centimeters tall. What is the volume of the solid?
questions.solution: The second prism has volume $5 \times 4 \times 3 = 60$ cubic centimeters. Adding the first, $60 + 60 = 120$ cubic centimeters.

questions.skill: Missing dimension from the volume
questions.stem: A rectangular prism has a volume of 120 cubic centimeters. It is 6 centimeters long and 5 centimeters wide. How many centimeters tall is it?
questions.solution: The base has area $6 \times 5 = 30$ square centimeters. Since volume is base area times height, the height is $120 \div 30 = 4$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Missing dimension from the volume
questions.stem: A box has a volume of 90 cubic feet and its base has an area of 15 square feet. How many feet tall is the box?
questions.solution: Volume is base area times height, so the height is $90 \div 15 = 6$ feet.

questions.skill: Volume as addition
questions.stem: The base of a tank is 40 centimeters by 25 centimeters. Water fills the tank to a height of 12 centimeters. Then 2000 more cubic centimeters of water are poured in. What is the volume of the water in the tank now, in cubic centimeters?
questions.solution: The first water has volume $40 \times 25 \times 12 = 12{,}000$ cubic centimeters. Adding the 2,000 poured in: $12{,}000 + 2{,}000 = 14{,}000$ cubic centimeters.

solve.work: 40 x 25 x 12 = 12000; 12000 + 2000 = 14000. (Tank height not given; it is assumed not to overflow.)

questions.skill: Volume of two joined prisms
questions.stem: A solid is made of two prisms joined along a face. The first is 4 by 5 by 6 and the second is 3 by 5 by 6, where the 5 by 6 faces are joined. Which expression gives the volume of the whole solid?
questions.solution: The two prisms share the same 5 by 6 face, so together they are one prism that is $4 + 3 = 7$ long, 5 wide and 6 tall. Its volume is $(4 + 3) \times 5 \times 6$, which is the same as $4 \times 5 \times 6 + 3 \times 5 \times 6$.

solve.work: 4x5x6 + 3x5x6 = (4+3) x 5 x 6 = 210 by the distributive property.

questions.skill: Volume formula length x width x height
questions.stem: A box is 15 centimeters long, 12 centimeters wide, and 8 centimeters tall. What is its volume in cubic centimeters?
questions.solution: $15 \times 12 = 180$, and $180 \times 8 = 1{,}440$. The volume is 1,440 cubic centimeters.

questions.skill: Volume as addition
questions.stem: A solid is built in two layers of unit cubes. The bottom layer is 6 cubes by 5 cubes. The top layer is 6 cubes by 2 cubes. How many unit cubes are in the solid?
questions.solution: The bottom layer has $6 \times 5 = 30$ cubes and the top layer has $6 \times 2 = 12$ cubes. Together: $30 + 12 = 42$. Treating both layers as the bottom layer would give 60.

questions.skill: Missing dimension from the volume
questions.stem: The volume of a rectangular prism is 72 cubic units. Which could be its length, width, and height?
questions.solution: Multiply each set: $6 \times 4 \times 3 = 72$, but $6 \times 4 \times 4 = 96$, $9 \times 4 \times 3 = 108$ and $8 \times 3 \times 4 = 96$. Only length 6, width 4, height 3 gives 72.

questions.skill: Volume of two joined prisms
questions.stem: A model of a building is made from two rectangular prisms joined together. The main part is 12 centimeters long, 8 centimeters wide, and 5 centimeters tall. The tower on top is 4 centimeters long, 4 centimeters wide, and 6 centimeters tall. What is the volume of the model in cubic centimeters?
questions.solution: The main part has volume $12 \times 8 \times 5 = 480$. The tower has volume $4 \times 4 \times 6 = 96$. Together: $480 + 96 = 576$ cubic centimeters.

questions.skill: Name a point as an ordered pair
questions.stem: Point $P$ is 4 units to the right of the origin and 7 units up. Which ordered pair names $P$?
questions.solution: The first number says how far to go right and the second how far to go up. Right 4 and up 7 is $(4, 7)$.

questions.skill: Name a point as an ordered pair
questions.stem: A point is named $(6, 2)$. How many units up from the origin is the point?
questions.solution: In an ordered pair the first number is the distance right and the second number is the distance up. So the point is 2 units up.

questions.skill: Name a point as an ordered pair
questions.stem: In the ordered pair $(3, 8)$, what does the 3 tell you?
choices: Move 3 units right from the origin
Move 3 units up from the origin
Move 8 units right from the origin
Move 8 units up from the origin
questions.answer: Move 3 units right from the origin
questions.solution: The first number of an ordered pair tells how many units to move right, along the x-axis, from the origin. So the 3 means move 3 units right.

solve.answer: Move 3 units right from the origin
solve.work: First coordinate is the horizontal distance: 3 units right.

questions.skill: Axes and the origin
questions.stem: Which ordered pair names the origin?
questions.solution: The origin is where the two axes meet. It is 0 units right and 0 units up, so it is $(0, 0)$.

questions.skill: Axes and the origin
questions.stem: A point is on the x-axis and 5 units to the right of the origin. What is its y-coordinate?
questions.solution: A point on the x-axis has not moved up at all, so its y-coordinate is 0. The point is $(5, 0)$.

solve.work: On the x-axis, y = 0. Point is (5, 0).

questions.skill: Move from a point
questions.stem: Start at the point $(2, 3)$ and move 4 units to the right. What is the x-coordinate of the new point?
questions.solution: Moving right adds to the x-coordinate: $2 + 4 = 6$. The new point is $(6, 3)$.

questions.skill: Distance between points on a grid line
questions.stem: Point $A$ is at $(1, 5)$ and point $B$ is at $(7, 5)$. How many units apart are $A$ and $B$?
questions.solution: Both points have y-coordinate 5, so they are on the same horizontal line. The distance is the difference of the x-coordinates: $7 - 1 = 6$.

questions.skill: Name a point as an ordered pair
questions.stem: Which of these points is farthest to the right?
questions.solution: How far right a point is depends on its first number, the x-coordinate. The first numbers are 2, 5, 8 and 4, and 8 is the largest.

questions.skill: Coordinates in a map or story
questions.stem: On a grid map, a park is at $(5, 2)$. A school is 3 units directly above the park. What is the y-coordinate of the school?
questions.solution: Directly above means the x-coordinate stays 5 and the y-coordinate goes up by 3: $2 + 3 = 5$. The school is at $(5, 5)$.

questions.skill: Axes and the origin
questions.stem: Point $Q$ is at $(0, 5)$. Where is $Q$?
choices: On the x-axis, 5 units right of the origin
On the y-axis, 5 units right of the origin
On the y-axis, 5 units up from the origin
questions.answer: On the y-axis, 5 units up from the origin
questions.solution: The x-coordinate is 0, so the point has not moved right. It is 5 units straight up from the origin, which puts it on the y-axis.

solve.answer: On the y-axis, 5 units up from the origin
solve.work: x = 0, so on the y-axis, 5 units up.

questions.skill: Name a point as an ordered pair
questions.stem: Dev plots a point by moving 5 units up from the origin and then 2 units to the right. Which ordered pair names the point?
questions.solution: The ordered pair always lists right first, then up. Dev went 2 right and 5 up, so the point is $(2, 5)$, even though he moved up first.

questions.skill: Name a point as an ordered pair
questions.stem: The x-coordinate of a point is 3 more than its y-coordinate. Its y-coordinate is 4. What is its x-coordinate?
questions.solution: The x-coordinate is 3 more than 4, so it is $4 + 3 = 7$. The point is $(7, 4)$.

questions.skill: Axes and the origin
questions.stem: Which of these points lies on the y-axis?
questions.solution: Every point on the y-axis has x-coordinate 0, since it has not moved right. Only $(0, 6)$ fits.

questions.skill: Axes and the origin
questions.stem: Which statement about the point $(4, 0)$ is true?
choices: It is on the y-axis, 4 units from the origin
It is on the x-axis, 4 units from the origin
It is at the origin, where the axes meet
It is 4 units above the x-axis
questions.answer: It is on the x-axis, 4 units from the origin
questions.solution: The y-coordinate is 0, so the point is on the x-axis. It is 4 units right of the origin.

solve.answer: It is on the x-axis, 4 units from the origin
solve.work: y = 0, x = 4: on the x-axis 4 units from origin.

questions.skill: Move from a point
questions.stem: A bug starts at $(3, 2)$. It crawls 5 units to the right and then 4 units up. Where does it stop?
questions.solution: Moving right adds 5 to the x-coordinate: $3 + 5 = 8$. Moving up adds 4 to the y-coordinate: $2 + 4 = 6$. The bug stops at $(8, 6)$.

questions.skill: Distance between points on a grid line
questions.stem: Points $C$ and $D$ are at $(2, 3)$ and $(2, 11)$. How many units apart are they?
questions.solution: Both points have x-coordinate 2, so they are on the same vertical line. The distance is the difference of the y-coordinates: $11 - 3 = 8$.

questions.skill: Distance between points on a grid line
questions.stem: Which pair of points lies on the same vertical line and is exactly 5 units apart?
questions.solution: Points on a vertical line share the same x-coordinate. $(2, 2)$ and $(2, 7)$ share x = 2 and their y-coordinates differ by $7 - 2 = 5$. The pair with $(7, 2)$ is 5 apart but on a horizontal line, and the pair with $(2, 5)$ is only 3 apart.

solve.work: Vertical line: same x. (2,2),(2,5): 3 apart. (2,2),(2,7): 5 apart. Others not vertical.

questions.skill: Missing corner of a rectangle or square
questions.stem: Three corners of a rectangle are $(1, 1)$, $(6, 1)$ and $(6, 4)$. What is the x-coordinate of the fourth corner?
questions.solution: The fourth corner is directly above $(1, 1)$ and level with $(6, 4)$, so it is $(1, 4)$. Its x-coordinate is 1.

solve.work: Rectangle with sides on x = 1, x = 6, y = 1, y = 4; missing corner (1, 4); x = 1.

questions.skill: Missing corner of a rectangle or square
questions.stem: A rectangle has corners at $(2, 2)$, $(2, 7)$ and $(9, 7)$. What is the fourth corner?
questions.solution: The missing corner is level with $(2, 2)$ (so its y-coordinate is 2) and directly below $(9, 7)$ (so its x-coordinate is 9). It is $(9, 2)$.

solve.work: x values 2 and 9, y values 2 and 7; missing corner (9, 2).

questions.skill: Coordinates in a map or story
questions.stem: On a map grid, each unit is 1 kilometer. A school is at $(3, 8)$ and a library is at $(3, 2)$. How many kilometers is it from the school straight down to the library?
questions.solution: The two places have the same x-coordinate, so the trip is straight down. The distance is $8 - 2 = 6$ kilometers.

questions.skill: Move from a point
questions.stem: A game piece starts at $(2, 9)$. It moves 3 units right, then 5 units down, then 4 units right. What is the y-coordinate of the point where it stops?
questions.solution: Only the move down changes the y-coordinate: $9 - 5 = 4$. (The piece ends at $(9, 4)$, since $2 + 3 + 4 = 9$.)

solve.work: y: 9 - 5 = 4 (right moves do not change y). Final (9, 4).

questions.skill: Move from a point
questions.stem: A point moves from $(3, 8)$ to $(7, 5)$. Which describes the move?
questions.solution: The x-coordinate goes from 3 to 7, which is 4 units to the right. The y-coordinate goes from 8 to 5, which is 3 units down.

questions.skill: Move from a point
questions.stem: A point at $(3, 5)$ is moved to the right and then up until it is at $(9, 12)$. How many units did it move in all?
questions.solution: It moved right $9 - 3 = 6$ units and up $12 - 5 = 7$ units. In all that is $6 + 7 = 13$ units.

questions.skill: Distance between points on a grid line
questions.stem: A rectangular garden has corners at $(2, 1)$, $(8, 1)$, $(8, 5)$ and $(2, 5)$. Each unit on the grid is 1 meter. What is the distance around the garden, in meters?
questions.solution: The bottom side runs from x = 2 to x = 8, so it is 6 meters. The side runs from y = 1 to y = 5, so it is 4 meters. The distance around is $2 \times (6 + 4) = 20$ meters.

questions.skill: Distance between points on a grid line
questions.stem: Point $A$ is at $(4, 2)$. Point $B$ is on the same horizontal line as $A$, 6 units from $A$ and to the right of it. Which is point $B$?
questions.solution: Staying on the same horizontal line keeps the y-coordinate at 2. Going 6 units right changes the x-coordinate to $4 + 6 = 10$. So $B$ is $(10, 2)$.

questions.skill: Missing corner of a rectangle or square
questions.stem: Three corners of a rectangle are $(3, 2)$, $(3, 8)$ and $(11, 2)$. What is the area of the rectangle, in square units?
questions.solution: One side runs from y = 2 to y = 8, so it is 6 units long. The other runs from x = 3 to x = 11, so it is 8 units long. The area is $6 \times 8 = 48$ square units.

questions.skill: Missing corner of a rectangle or square
questions.stem: A square has one corner at $(4, 4)$ and sides 5 units long that run to the right and up from that corner. Which point is the corner opposite $(4, 4)$?
questions.solution: Going 5 units right and 5 units up from $(4, 4)$ reaches $(9, 9)$. The points $(9, 4)$ and $(4, 9)$ are the two corners next to $(4, 4)$.

questions.skill: Coordinates in a map or story
questions.stem: Zoe walks along a straight street from the bakery at $(4, 6)$ to the library at $(10, 6)$. Then she walks straight to the park at $(10, 2)$. Each unit is 1 block. How many blocks does she walk in all?
questions.solution: The first part is along a horizontal line: $10 - 4 = 6$ blocks. The second part is along a vertical line: $6 - 2 = 4$ blocks. In all she walks $6 + 4 = 10$ blocks.

questions.skill: Coordinates in a map or story
questions.stem: On a grid map each unit is 1 mile. The cafe is at $(2, 5)$, the gym is at $(2, 12)$ and the pool is at $(8, 5)$. Which statement is true?
choices: The pool is 1 mile farther from the cafe than the gym is
The gym and the pool are the same distance from the cafe
The gym is 7 miles farther from the cafe than the pool is
The gym is 1 mile farther from the cafe than the pool is
questions.answer: The gym is 1 mile farther from the cafe than the pool is
questions.solution: The gym is straight up from the cafe: $12 - 5 = 7$ miles. The pool is straight across: $8 - 2 = 6$ miles. So the gym is $7 - 6 = 1$ mile farther away.

solve.answer: The gym is 1 mile farther from the cafe than the pool is
solve.work: Gym: 12 - 5 = 7 mi; pool: 8 - 2 = 6 mi. Gym is 1 mile farther.

questions.skill: Coordinates in a map or story
questions.stem: A treasure is hidden 8 units right of the y-axis and 5 units up from the x-axis. A second treasure is 3 units to the right of the first, at the same distance from the x-axis. What is the x-coordinate of the second treasure?
questions.solution: The first treasure is at $(8, 5)$. Moving 3 units to the right at the same height gives $(11, 5)$, so the x-coordinate is 11.
